Commentary.Commentary: See you later! A commanding performance from South Africa, who walk away with a massive, one-sided victory! The 2026 T20 World Cup action doesn't stop here, though, as we have a huge triple-header lined up for Tuesday, February 10th as well. We’ll kick things off early with the Netherlands facing Namibia in New Delhi at 5.30 am GMT, followed by New Zealand taking on the UAE in Chennai, and finally, we wrap up the day with Pakistan going against the USA in the Sri Lankan capital of Colombo. Make sure to tune in for the pre-match build-up tomorrow. Until then, take care and goodbye!

The victorious captain of South Africa - Aiden Markram admits that the early stages of the competition have shown that anyone can beat anyone, stressing that no opposition can be taken lightly. Adds that he is pleased with the start from his side. Also mentions that selection calls aren’t easy, but adds that the players missing out have taken it well and continue to bring strong energy to the group. He points out that the death overs are a crucial phase in India and feels Miller and Stubbs managed it smartly, doing the hard work initially before teeing off later. Markram also praises the bowlers for their effort, noting there was a little assistance up front before the dew set in. Details that they continued to ask questions throughout the innings. Looking ahead to Afghanistan, the semifinalists from the last edition, he highlights the challenge of a day game and wraps by stressing that his side would need to be right on it.

The captain of Canada - Dilpreet Bajwa says that they were expecting to chase 170-175, but admits that they leaked extra runs in the death overs. On Ansh Patel, he says that he bowled well and also praises Dhaliwal for his excellent knock. Specifically mentions that Dhaliwal's 10 years of experience playing for Canada has helped them massively. Admits that they are lacking experience as they don't play against big teams. Mentions that South Africa's bowlers are top class and Canada did well with the bat. Ends by saying that they lost early wickets and stresses on watching the ball properly moving ahead.
Let's hear what the captains have to say...

PLAYER OF THE MATCH - Lungi Ngidi gets the award for bowling figures of 4/31 in 4 overs. On being asked about what it is that brings the best out of him in this format, he puts it down to his willingness to take wickets. Adds that he likes to take risks and also admits that sometimes he goes for boundaries, but sometimes those balls pay off and reward him with wickets too. Reflecting on the game plan against players they hadn't faced before, he admits it was one of the areas they struggled with on the night. Adds that it became a case of trial and error as the innings progressed, with some deliveries disappearing for boundaries and that the plans were adjusted following discussions in the middle. He feels things were fairly straightforward with the new ball, but after that, it largely came down to experimentation.  Speaking about the impact of dew, he agrees that it did play a part, especially when the ball was bowled a touch fuller, as it tended to skid on. Details, while the slower deliveries still held up a bit, the ball generally came on better to the bat, and a few clean connections confirmed that the dew was having an effect. He adds that although their attack is built around pace, it's the variations that tend to catch batters out. His own approach, he says, is to keep things simple, to hit good lengths, change the pace, and keep batters guessing.

Miller and Stubbs provided a late flourish - Earlier in the game, South Africa laid a solid foundation, racing to 65 without loss in the Powerplay. Aiden Markram anchored the innings beautifully with a well-compiled fifty, but Ansh Patel briefly pulled things back for Canada, reducing the heavyweights to 138/4. However, the death overs belonged to David Miller and Tristan Stubbs. The duo forged an unbeaten 75-run stand, smashing 62 runs in the last five overs, to propel the score to a daunting 213/4.

Dhaliwal fought till the end! While the result was evident, Navneet Dhaliwal and Harsh Thaker showed great character, stitching together a 69-run partnership to steady the ship. Dhaliwal played a lone hand with a gritty 64, but he lacked support from the other end. Lungi Ngidi was the wrecker-in-chief, tearing through the top order to finish with a four-wicket haul, while Marco Jansen chipped in with two scalps. Ultimately, Canada finished well short, handing South Africa a comprehensive win.

Top order crumbled for Canada - Chasing a mountain of 214 was always going to be a tall order, and Canada’s hopes took a massive hit immediately. Skipper Dilpreet Bajwa departed for a golden duck on the very first ball, setting the tone for a shaky start. The South African pacers were relentless, leaving Canada reeling at 50/4 by the end of the Powerplay. The required rate kept climbing, and the constant fall of wickets meant the chase never really took off.

A convincing win for the Proteas! South Africa have started their T20 World Cup 2026 campaign with a bang, registering a convincing 57-run victory. As the runners-up from the last edition, the Proteas looked every bit the favorites, dominating proceedings from the very first ball. Despite a spirited effort in patches from Canada, they fell way short as South Africa picked up two crucial points.

FOUR! Well-struck. Short of a good length, around the off pole. Kaleem Sana stands tall, hits through the line and smashes it over extra cover for a cracking boundary. SOUTH AFRICA BEAT CANADA BY 57 RUNS!

Commentary.Commentary: End of the Powerplay. Canada are teetering at 50/4, and at the same stage, South Africa were motoring along with 66/0 on the board. Corbin Bosch is introduced into the attack.

Good follow-up delivery. Nips in from off, on a length, Harsh Thaker inside edges on the thigh pad while looking to nudge it around the corner. The ball deflects away to mid-wicket and they cross over. 50 up for Canada!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Top shot! Full from Rabada, outside off, Harsh Thaker opens the bat face right at the point of contact and threads it through the point and backward point fielders for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.5: Kagiso Rabada to Harsh Thaker, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: DRINKS BREAK. The Proteas are ruling over the roost in Ahmedabad. Kagiso Rabada and Lungi Ngidi have provided an extremely strong start for them. Canada need to calm down a bit and form a steady partnership. The need is to bat long and consolidate the middle overs to get them out of jail. South Africa will look to keep their knee pressed on the throat of the opposition and just not allow them any momentum. Harsh Thaker walks in at number 6.

OUT! BOWLED! Corker of a delivery from Rabada and the off stump goes for a walk. He nails in a yorker, which lands at the base of the off stump. Shreyas Movva plays from the crease without moving his feet and tries to work it across with a flick, but ends up playing all over it. The ball goes past the inside edge and uproots the off stump. Shreyas Movva departs on 9 (11) and Canada are 45/4, needing 169 more.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.4: Kagiso Rabada to Shreyas Movva, OUT! b Kagiso Rabada.

Commentary.Commentary: Sharp nip-backer, on a good length, Shreyas Movva dinks it to the mid-wicket region.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.3: Kagiso Rabada to Shreyas Movva, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Absolute beauty! Slams the deck hard, and it nips in with good bounce on top of off. Shreyas Movva hops on the toes to block but plays inside the line and the ball whistles past the outside edge.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.2: Kagiso Rabada to Shreyas Movva, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh this one skids through, on middle, Navneet Dhaliwal jams the bat down and the ball squirts off the inner half to deep backward square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 5.1: Kagiso Rabada to Navneet Dhaliwal, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: A low full toss, on middle, Shreyas Movva flicks it to the mid on fielder. A dot to end the over.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.6: Lungi Ngidi to Shreyas Movva, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: On a length, on off, Shreyas Movva looks to block it but edges it to the fielder at short third. Dot again.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.5: Lungi Ngidi to Shreyas Movva, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, dear! Lungi Ngidi slipped badly on his follow-through and landed pretty hard onto the pitch while trying to pluck the ball to his right. He is down on the ground and the physio rushes out to check him up. He is being helped with a couple of several stretching exercises before he is good to go.

Uppish but safe! Length, on off, Shreyas Movva looks to block it but the ball hits the upper part of his bat. The ball lobs for a bit and lands safely towards the mid on fielder. Lungi Ngidi falls to his right in the process of perhaps taking the catch. He looks in some pain.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.4: Lungi Ngidi to Shreyas Movva, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Nice and full, targeting the stumps. Shreyas Movva covers his line and blocks it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.3: Lungi Ngidi to Shreyas Movva, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR MORE! A hat trick of boundaries now for Canada! On a length, outside off, Shreyas Movva uses the pace of the ball and steers it through backward point for yet another boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.2: Lungi Ngidi to Shreyas Movva, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Nicely played! Lungi Ngidi errs his line down the leg side, Shreyas Movva uses the pace of the ball and tickles it through fine leg for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Lungi Ngidi to Shreyas Movva, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Wow, what a shot from Navneet Dhaliwal! Back of a length, on off, Navneet Dhaliwal hops a bit and punches it in the gap through point for a boundary. That was brilliant timing.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Kagiso Rabada to Navneet Dhaliwal, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: The chase is spiralling downward for the Canadians now. Shreyas Movva is the next batter in at number 5.

OUT! TAKEN! Lungi Ngidi gets his third wicket. Back of a length, on off, Nicholas Kirton rocks back and tries to loft it but mistimes his stroke completely off the splice of the blade. The ball spoons towards mid on. Kagiso Rabada dives forward and takes a good catch at the edge of the circle. The South Africans are up and about with broad smiles, and why not? Canada are in a spot of bother. They are reduced to 26/3 after 3 overs!
Commentary.Howout: c Kagiso Rabada b Lungi Ngidi
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Lungi Ngidi to Nicholas Kirton, OUT! c Kagiso Rabada b Lungi Ngidi.

Commentary.Commentary: A promising start for the Proteas as they have dismissed both Canadian openers inside the first three overs. In walks Nicholas Kirton at number 4.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! What a delivery from Lungi Ngidi. On a length and this one comes in and nips away at the last moment. Yuvraj Samra tries to block but his feet go nowhere. He hangs his bat loosely away from the body without much conviction and gets a faint edge and Quinton de Kock completes the catch. Lungi Ngidi gets his second wicket. Canada are 22/2 after 2.3 overs.
Commentary.Howout: c Quinton de Kock b Lungi Ngidi
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Lungi Ngidi to Yuvraj Samra, OUT! c Quinton de Kock b Lungi Ngidi.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! A beautiful cover drive from Yuvraj Samra! Touch fuller, outside off, Yuvraj Samra leans on and cracks a drive through cover for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Lungi Ngidi to Yuvraj Samra, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Oh, close! But safe. Hits the deck hard, does Ngidi. It is angling around off, and Navneet taps it to the left of backward point. The fielder dives to his left and gets rid of the ball as there is a bit of yes yes and no no between the batters. The direct hit is scored, but not before Navneet plonks his bat inside the crease, rather than dragging it in. The ball ricochets to the backward square leg region and seeing that, the batters do pinch in a quick run.

OUT! CAUGHT BEHIND! Lungi Ngidi strikes first ball. A golden duck for the Canada skipper. On a length, on off, in the channel of uncertainty, and it shapes away from the right-hander. Dilpreet Bajwa gets a bit indecisive about whether to play or leave. Decides to leave it but he is a bit too late in doing so and in the process, he gets a feather. Quinton de Kock behind the stumps makes no mistake. The appeal goes around and up goes the finger. Canada are 0/1, chasing 214.
Commentary.Howout: c Quinton de Kock b Lungi Ngidi
